evidence.curator_note: First arrow of Equation 8.67. CONCRETE scheme: the piperidine molecular ion, n-ionized at nitrogen ('+.' written next to the ring N, which also carries an explicit H). Atom maps: 1 = N, 2 = C2 (becomes the CH2 of the iminium head), 3 = C3 (becomes the radical terminus), 4 = C4, 5 = C5, 6 = C6 (the other N-adjacent carbon, which donates H map 7). Alpha-cleavage forms the N1=C2 iminium bond and breaks the C2-C3 ring bond, opening the ring to the distonic ion CH2=N+(H)-CH2CH2CH2-.CH2 that the page draws as the middle structure (radical dot on the far chain terminus). Book draws 2 arcs: the small fishhook leaving the N '+.' dot and hooking down onto the N-C2 bond (move <1>), and the large fishhook whose tail sits on the C2-C3 ring bond and whose barb points back at the forming N=C2 bond (move <2>); move <3>, the other C2-C3 sigma electron onto C3, is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page, although the product radical dot is shown).

Second arrow of Equation 8.67, drawn on the folded ring-opened intermediate. The explicitly drawn H (map 7) on C6 - the carbon still bonded to N - is transferred across the folded chain to the C3 radical terminus, and the products printed on the page are the even-electron ion CH2=N+(H)-CH=CH2 labelled 'm/z 56' plus the ethyl radical drawn as H2C(.)-CH3, i.e. C2H5. loss. Book draws 2 arcs, both fishhooks: one whose tail sits on the C6-H bond and whose barb points across to the radical carbon (move <2>, one C6-H electron travelling with the H into the new C3-H bond), and one whose tail is at the radical dot on C3 and whose barb points back at the H (move <1>, the C3 odd electron into that same new bond). Moves <3,4,5> are implicit and required for electron balance (not drawn on the page): <3> the other C6-H electron into the forming C5=C6 pi bond, <4> one electron of the breaking C4-C5 sigma bond into that same pi bond, and <5> the other C4-C5 electron onto C4, which becomes the radical carbon of the expelled ethyl radical. COMPOSITE-STEP DISCLOSURE: the two DRAWN arcs by themselves only perform the 1,4-H shift and would stop at an undrawn C6-radical intermediate CH2=N+(H)-.CH-CH2CH2CH3; the beta-scission of C4-C5 that actually produces the printed products is not drawn as arcs and the book draws no structure for that intermediate, so - rather than invent an undrawn species - the H shift and the beta-scission are encoded as one composite step whose five moves reproduce exactly the products printed on the page.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.67 (its chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14), so no MOD rule variable is cross-linked. Candidates checked and REJECTED: (i) IMS_4_9 'radical induced (alpha-)clevage for a saturated site', DFS [C]1[C]2[C]3([C]4)[_A+.]5>>[C.]1.[C]2[C]3([C]4){=}[_A+.]5, is the only generic saturated-heteroatom alpha-cleavage rule in the index, but it cleaves C1-C2, a bond NOT incident to C3, the atom that forms the new pi bond to the heteroatom, so it does not describe the N1=C2 / C2-C3 bond change of this scheme; it also leaves [_A+.] on the product heteroatom while creating [C.]1 (one unpaired electron becomes two), failing the L->R spin conservation that the rules/__init__.py guardrail enforces, so it is auto-dropped from the fragmentation list anyway. (ii) IMS_8_6_1..IMS_8_6_4, the only indexed ring-fragmentation family, act on an all-carbon cyclooctadiene-type ring with no heteroatom and no H migration. (iii) hTransition_saturated_2 / hTransition_saturated_2_alpha move an H onto a carbon radical in a chain carrying a charged site, which is the closest analogue of the second step, but they deposit the resulting unsaturation and charge differently (they regenerate a [_A+.] heteroatom radical cation rather than the even-electron conjugated iminium printed here), so they are not cross-linked either. PROVENANCE OF THE MS CONTEXT: the page names no ionization conditions; it states only that for piperidine this C2H5. loss 'produces the second most-intense peak', which in this book means the standard 70 eV EI spectrum of the molecular ion, and ms_context is set accordingly.

'm/z 56' is printed under the product ion on the page, so the ion is flagged detected=true and the assignment status is 'proposed'. NO percentage is printed for it - the running text only calls it 'the second most-intense peak' - so relative_intensity is deliberately omitted rather than guessed. observed_mz 56.0495 is the monoisotopic m/z of C3H6N+ (CH2=N+H-CH=CH2), consistent with the printed nominal 56 and with loss of C2H5. (29) from the m/z 85.089 molecular ion. The same text warns that much of the m/z 56 from piperidine could instead arise by H loss followed by RDA loss of C2H4 (Equation 8.61), i.e. this assignment is one of two competing routes to the peak.
